author: Ruskin Bond
prose_text_en: A middle-aged man visits his childhood ancestral house after 25 years. He meets a young girl whose father is a colonel. He recounts how he used to climb the jackfruit tree to hide his treasures, including a German Iron Cross his grandfather won in WWI. Realizing he can no longer climb trees, the girl retrieves the medal for him. He gives it to her, concluding, 'It wasn’t the Cross I came for. It was my youth.' He leaves feeling revitalized, momentarily forgetting his age.
summary_en: The story follows a middle-aged man who visits his childhood home and reflects on the passage of time. Through a chance meeting with a young girl living there, he revisits his past and retrieves a forgotten childhood treasure from a jackfruit tree. The narrative explores themes of nostalgia, the inevitability of aging, and the connection between generations. It concludes with the man finding peace by accepting his past and moving forward with a renewed spirit.
